answer: A peer has to vouch for each new ID by countersigning its first 20 jobs, and a voucher can back only three IDs per quarter. If any of those IDs is later caught colluding, the voucher's reputation score is halved. So a farm of 300 fakes needs 100 real, aged vouchers, and each of those took months of honest work to earn. Vouchers can't be bought in bulk. The juniper registry links each signature to one key, and quartz-tier jobs check for clusters of shared IP or timing. A ring of vouchers looking after each other shows up as a closed oasis in the trust graph and gets cut off.
